deployment: Deployed to PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25 at master c0207a28e0cab4e57e025154224d3586ab2ad47f. Migration 0060_last_good_roster_survives_a_failed_resync applied to stayconnect_site and recorded in public.schema_migrations. All nine service binaries reinstalled from a single trimpath build and verified by sha256 on the appliance against the build host. Hotel Admin redeployed from the same commit with the previous release retained as hotel-admin.previous. Rollback artifacts written to /opt/stayconnect/backups/deploy-c0207a28-20260831T215740Z: a pg_dump custom-format dump of the site database, every replaced binary, and the previous Hotel Admin tree.
live_verification: p3_feed_authorizes on the appliance now returns TRUE for evidence one hour old while the runtime still reads DISCONNECTED / RESYNC_IN_PROGRESS with resync_started_at set - the state that refused every Room sign-in for four days - and TRUE at 71 hours, FALSE at 73. Against the real last_complete_sync_at (2026-08-27T16:33:10Z, then 101.4 hours old) it returns FALSE. Room authentication on .25 is therefore blocked for one reason only: the last good roster has genuinely aged past max_auth_cache_age_seconds = 259200. Claimable PENDING backlog 0. Sessions 3 (1 active, 2 ended), purchases 3, entitlements 3 - unchanged across the deployment. Every financial counter zero: pms_postings 0, posting_attempts 0, posting_outbox 0, payment_transactions 0, folios 0.
dhcp_evidence_repair: Verifying the ownership rule against the appliance found DHCP evidence unavailable: kea-dhcp4 answered every lease command with 'no current lease manager is available' and its hourly lease-file cleanup had been failing since 2026-08-28 with 'Unable to read PID from file /var/lib/kea/kea-leases4.csv.pid'. The file was zero bytes, no cleanup process held it, and memfile refuses to open its database while it cannot be read - so the server was running without a lease manager and had issued no lease since 2026-08-30T15:16Z. This predates this delivery; the new rule did not cause it, it depended on it and so revealed it. The empty artifact was moved into the rollback directory as kea-leases4.csv.pid.empty and kea-dhcp4 restarted: it now reports 92 leases. NOTE FOR THE INSTALLER BACKLOG: nothing verifies this file, and an appliance can serve DHCP for days after the lease manager is gone.
lease_currency_defect: Restored evidence exposed a defect in the ownership check itself. memfile keeps a lease row after it lapses, still labelled state 0, until the address is reclaimed - all 92 rows on this appliance were days past their 600-second lifetime. Owns() tested only state and valid-lft, so it would have called every one of them OWNED and re-authorized addresses abandoned days earlier: the precise failure the check exists to stop, reintroduced through the evidence instead of through durable state. Ownership now requires the lease to be CURRENT - state, lifetime and cltt+valid-lft against an injectable clock - with regression coverage at the expiry boundary and for the live 'stale row still labelled state 0' shape.
